name: Why does kitchen drywall installation in older Denver-area homes require extra prep?

mainEntity.name: Why does kitchen drywall installation in older Denver-area homes require extra prep?

acceptedAnswer.text: In older homes across the Denver metro area, including communities like Arvada, Englewood, and Littleton, kitchens often have uneven framing, settling, or original plaster walls. Hanging new drywall on out-of-plumb studs will cause noticeable alignment issues when installing modern, rigid kitchen cabinets and stone countertops. Contractors working in these homes must frequently sister new studs, shim low spots, or plane high spots before hanging drywall to ensure flat, square surfaces. Additionally, local Denver climate conditions with low indoor winter humidity require proper joint compound drying management to prevent seam cracking.
acceptedAnswer.description: Older Denver homes often feature uneven framing or plaster settling. Studs must be shimmed or planed flat before hanging drywall so new cabinets and countertops hang level.
